limits: POSIX local-filesystem opt-in library; missing/corrupt namespaces fail closed.
A persisted success receipt means callback success was recorded, not current file state or atomicity of file and log.
In-flight records cannot distinguish a still-running worker from an interrupted one; no re-execution.
Same-ID reservation spans cooperating processes sharing one journal. Different-ID file locks remain process-local.
Directory allocation lock is not stolen after a crash. Owner review is required before any recovery.
No automatic eviction, retry, rollback, PID killing or namespace reset.
Stores relative-path receipts and digests, not file contents, source edits or exception messages. Hashes are not confidentiality encryption.
Directory/file fsync requests are OS/device dependent and SIGKILL does not simulate power failure.
Existing remote E0/E1 evidence is preserved and does not apply automatically to unpublished local code.
